title: Keeping an AI-made game cohesive across five chapters: what we did differently on our second game
author: Zealousideal-Bar-316
selftext:
Pixel & Pincel is a 2-player co-op platformer from a small team in Brazil (we also make Caçarola). One hero is pixel art, the other is gouache paint, and every level needs both: she paints bridges in the air, he freezes them; her paint reveals the monsters, his square freezes them, his punch shatters them.



Our first game was about speed. On this one we spent almost three weeks and most of that time went into cohesion:



\- Code: Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (Godot 4.7, \~15k lines). Before the final chapter it audited every mechanic for repetition, and the last chapter uses only new ones.

\- Art: image generation for backgrounds, props and painted story panels. Every chapter started as concepts we chose from. Backgrounds are hand-composed painted layers per district, after a modular building kit looked too assembled.

\- Animation: PixelLab, 16 frames per action, always from an approved pose. The two heroes never change art style: Bit is always pixels, Guache is always paint.

\- Music and SFX: ElevenLabs, with one shared musical identity (same key, instruments and melody) across all 25 cues.

\- QA: bots play every chapter offline and online after each change, plus human playtests. A human still caught the worst bug: the heroine ran backwards in one direction.



The video is all in-engine footage plus a few painted story panels. No store page for this game yet; our Steam page is for Caçarola: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5370000/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5370000/)

comments.author: HomeTimeLegend
comments.body: It's a really good looking game, congratulations. Cacarola is a good looking game too! Kudos to your art direction.

replies.author: Zealousideal-Bar-316
replies.body: Thanks a lot!! We are trying to do better every time. Its not just developing games to win money, we love games and we want to bring a experience!
